a: The disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs are generally among the ambiguous matters whose true meaning only Allah knows; in them is an indication of the inimitability of the Qur’an: it is composed of the very letters of which the Arabs’ language consists. The Arabs’ inability to produce its like — though they were the most eloquent of people — shows that the Qur’an is revelation from Allah. Opinions on interpreting these letters are many and varied. They comprise fourteen letters of the Arabic alphabet and form the phrase: “A wise text with a decisive secret”; a group of interpreters said they are Allah’s secret in the Qur’an.

“O our people”: “yā” marks address; “people” here means a group of jinn.
“Respond to Allah’s caller”: answer him and follow him.
“Allah’s caller”: one urging worship of Him.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
‘Ba’: a preposition conveying the meaning of adherence (attachment).
‘Min’: a preposition indicating taking a thing from a thing, in the meaning of ‘ba‘d’ (part).
‘Dhunub’: plural of ‘dhanb’; a dhanb is a sin, a forbidden act.
A preposition conveying the meaning of the beginning of the extent.
‘Man’: a jussive conditional noun, specific to rational beings.
“Whoever does not respond to Allah’s caller”: whoever does not accept his call, believe in it or follow it.
“Allah’s caller”: one urging worship of Him.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
“Cannot escape on earth”: cannot flee or evade punishment.
A preposition conveying the meaning of literal spatial containment.
The well-known planet on whose surface we live, or a part of it.
‘Min’: a preposition conveying choice, or taking one thing in place of another.

Awliya’: plural of ‘wali’; and the ‘wali’ is one who is at your side in your sitting; what is meant: the nearest and most fitting in supporting you and defending you, or the one in charge of your affair and its custodian, who should bring you benefit and turn away harm from you.
A noun pointing to a group, followed by the ‘kaf’ of address for the masculine singular.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative containment.
Error: wandering, distance, and turning away from the path of guidance and truth.
Lam: a particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
“Have they not seen”: the expression urges consideration and conveys surprise at those spoken about; it addresses those who have seen, those who have heard and those who have neither seen nor heard.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.

A name of the Most High Essence, unique in divinity, whose existence is necessary, worshipped by right; it is the Word of Majesty (lafz al-jalalah) comprehending the meanings of all of Allah’s perfect attributes.
A relative noun for the masculine singular.
Brought into being without a prior model; and Allah’s creation is from nothingness.
The celestial bodies, and the upper world.
‘Al-ard’: the well-known planet on whose surface we live, or a part of it.
Lam: a particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
“Did not tire”: was not powerless and did not become fatigued.
By creating them without a prior model; Allah’s creation is from nothing.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
A verbal-noun particle conveying the future.
‘Give life to the dead’: grant them life.
‘Al-mawta’: those bereft of life, whose souls have been separated from their bodies.
A particle answering a question, conveying affirmation of what was negated.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
A word denoting comprehensiveness and total inclusion; it occurs in an explicit or implied possessive construction.
A thing: what can rightly be spoken of, whether sensory or abstract.
An attribute of Allah, glorified and exalted; al-Qadir is the One whom neither weakness nor languor touches; He is able to do all things and nothing renders Him incapable.
What is meant is one of the days of the punishment of Hell.
“The disbelievers are exposed to the Fire”: they are brought to it and see it.
A relative noun for a group of males.
They denied and did not believe.
‘Ala: a preposition conveying the meaning of literal superposition (being above).
The fire of the Hereafter, which is the fire of Hell.
‘Alaysa’: for affirmation, that is, to establish the attribution of its predicate to its subject.
A demonstrative for a nearby masculine singular referent; “hā’” draws attention.
A particle answering a question, conveying affirmation of what was negated.
And by our God whom we worship.
Tasting: the general sensation in which all sensory faculties participate.
‘Ma’: a verbal-noun particle that, together with what follows it, is interpreted as a verbal noun.
‘Kana’: usually comes as an incomplete verb to indicate the past; and it comes for remoteness or to transcend the temporal meaning in relation to Allah the Exalted.
So endure and do not despair.
Determination: firmly intending to carry out a matter; the messengers of firm resolve are said to be Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad, blessings and peace be upon them.
A preposition conveying clarification of the kind, or clarification of what is vague before ‘min’ or in its context.

‘Ar-rusul’ is the plural of ‘rasul’; a messenger among the angels is one who conveys the divine message from Allah, and a messenger among people is one whom Allah sends with a law to act upon it and convey it.
“And do not hasten”: do not rush the matter or request it quickly.
What is meant is the Day of Resurrection.
A particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
A particle of restriction; the exception here is called ‘emptied’ (mufarragh).
A portion of time with no exact duration intended.
A preposition conveying clarification of the kind, or clarification of what is vague before ‘min’ or in its context.
Day: the time from sunrise to sunset.
‘Hal’: a particle for asking about the content of the sentence; the question here is one of denial.
A particle of restriction; the exception here is called ‘emptied’ (mufarragh).
Qawm: a group of men and women.
The transgressors: the disobedient who go out of the bounds of the Sacred Law.
